hypothesis: A swarm of N diverse ~100k-parameter models gains capability exponentially in N: majority-vote error falls like exp(-cN) rather than as a power law N^-b.
intriguing: Error follows a clean power law (~N^-1.4) whose floor is set by shared mistakes: the same members with independent errors would be perfect by N=8.

criteria.name: Swarm beats its members
criteria.desc: Majority vote of 8 different members minus mean single-member accuracy
criteria.source: Li et al. 2024 (More Agents Is All You Need) report gains of this size on arithmetic/GSM8K

criteria.name: Error falls exponentially (the core claim)
criteria.desc: Exponential fit of log error vs N beats power-law fit (AIC difference, power - exp)
criteria.source: Condorcet jury theorem: independent voters give exponential error decay

criteria.name: Diversity, not count, drives it
criteria.desc: 8 different members voting minus 1 member sampled 8 times
criteria.source: Krogh & Vedelsby 1995: ensemble gain = member diversity (ambiguity)

criteria.name: Worth the compute
criteria.desc: Swarm of 4 (greedy vote) minus one member trained 4x longer (same training FLOPs)
criteria.source: Compute-matched baseline (Hoffmann et al. 2022 framing); 1-point tolerance

criteria.name: Adaptive stopping saves calls
criteria.desc: Adaptive (margin 2) accuracy within 1 pt of fixed N=8, using <= 4 calls/question
criteria.source: Aggarwal et al. 2023 (Adaptive-Consistency) report 3-6x fewer samples at <0.1 pt loss
